chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Ali ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man has from the optional prayers so many that he does not know what they are due to their abundance; what should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Let him pray until he does not know how many he has prayed due to their abundance, so he will have fulfilled by the measure of his knowledge.'

I said, 'Suppose he is not able to fulfill them due to many occupations?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is necessary, or a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him; and if his occupation is for the world, being preoccupied with it from the prayer, then upon him is the fulfillment, or else he will meet Allah as slighting, negligent, wasting the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

I said, 'Suppose he is not able to fulfill them, so would it be suitable for him to give charity?' So he was silent for a while, then said, 'Yes, let him give charity.' I said, 'And what should he give charity with?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'According to his capacity, and the least of that is a Mudd for each poor person in place of each prayer.'

I said, 'And how many prayers obligate upon him a Mudd for each poor person?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'For every two Rak'at from the night prayer, and every two Rak'at from the daytime prayer.'

So I said, 'He is not able.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'A Mudd for every four Rak'at.' I said, 'He is not able.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'A Mudd for every night prayer, and a Mudd for the daytime prayer, and the prayer is superior, and the prayer is superior.'

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific volume measurement for charity

ai.seo_question: How to make up for missed optional prayers when one cannot count them or perform them due to busy life?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'Qada bil-'Ilm' (making up by the measure of knowledge) for optional prayers, distinguishing between valid excuses like livelihood needs and valid excuses like worldly distraction. It establishes a graded system of compensation, where charity (Sadaqah) serves as a substitute for missed Nafl prayers, with specific measurements (a Mudd per poor person) linked to the number of Rak'at, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on maintaining spiritual discipline even when exact performance is impossible. The Imam’s final affirmation that 'Prayer is better' underscores the superior merit of actual worship over its monetary equivalent.
